No, that is not true. The Swiss Confederation did not adopt its first constitution in 1291, and no constitution from that time remains in force today.

The year 1291 is traditionally associated with the founding of the Old Swiss Confederacy through the Federal Charter (Bundesbrief), an alliance between the original cantons of Uri, Schwyz, and Unterwalden to protect their freedoms and mutual interests. However, this document was not a comprehensive constitution in the modern sense, but rather a pact between several communities. Moreover, it has undergone numerous revisions over the centuries.

Switzerland has adopted several constitutions over time. The current constitution of the Swiss Confederation entered into force on **18 April 1999**. Previous constitutions included those of 1802, 1848, and 1874. Therefore, the claim that the 1291 document remains unchanged is incorrect.
